title: Read an ADR from the tree, read-only
prompt:
# Story 4: Read an ADR from the tree, read-only

- **Story**: XXX-read-adr-from-builder
- **Created**: 2026-11-07
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: open `adrs`, press an ADR file, read it, and move to a driver from the tree.

## Story

As a team member, I want to open an ADR from the tree and read it, so that I can check a decision of my project from the builder, knowing
that I cannot change it there.

## Acceptance tests

- [ ] **Given** `adrs` is open, **When** the user presses an ADR file, **Then** everything of story 3 holds for it (the panel, the rail, "Show
  files", the two views, Close, and no control that edits), with these differences.
- [ ] **Given** the open ADR, **Then** the header shows the ADR icon and the path `adrs/0011-use-typescript-for-the-frontend.md`, and the lock
  says "Read-only here. Edit this ADR from the ADRs page."
- [ ] **Given** the ADR, **Then** its text is the Markdown stored for it, as it is: the title, the Status and Date lines, and the sections
  Context, Decision and Consequences. Nothing is added or taken out.
- [ ] **Given** an ADR of any status, **Then** it opens. **Given** a status that is none of the usual four, **Then** it opens all the same.
- [ ] **Given** an ADR with no text beyond its title, **Then** it shows that title, and no placeholder line.
- [ ] **Given** the user changed an ADR on the ADR page and opened the workspace again, **Then** the file shows the saved text.
- [ ] **Given** an ADR is open, **When** the user opens a driver, **Then** the driver takes its place, with its own icon and note, and the rail
  shows the icon of `drivers`. **Given** the other way round, **Then** the rail shows the icon of `adrs`.

## Business rules and constraints

- An ADR is immutable here. It is written on the ADR page, and nothing in the builder changes, moves, deletes or approves it. Which ADRs a
  story can link to (only the Accepted ones) is a rule of the stories, not of this tree.
- The file keeps the name it has in the repository, and its number and name never change when it is shown.

## Out of scope

- Writing, editing and changing the status of an ADR (`story-adrs.md`), and linking an ADR to a story or an enabler.
- Anything about stories and architectural enablers.

## Tasks

- [ ] Give the ADR the same file panel as a driver, with its own icon, path and read-only note.
- [ ] Show the stored Markdown of the ADR unchanged in both views.
- [ ] Make the rail show the icon of the folder of the file that is open, for both kinds.
- [ ] Test: an ADR of each status, an ADR with only a title, and the move between a driver and an ADR.

tasks.text: Extend the file-panel component in the `ui` layer to accept an ADR file type, rendering its icon, path, and read-only note distinct from a driver's (ADR-0007, AE-0002)
Wire the ADR selection in the builder tree to the existing read-ADR use case (or introduce a minimal one if absent), following the Clean Architecture inward-dependency rule (ADR-0007, AE-0002)
Display the stored ADR Markdown unchanged in both the rendered and raw-Markdown views, reusing the view-toggle already present for drivers (story 021)
Update the rail so it reflects the folder icon (`adrs` or `drivers`) of whichever file is currently open, covering the switch in both directions
Write Jest unit tests for the ViewModel: ADR with each of the four standard statuses, ADR with a non-standard status, ADR with only a title, and switching from a driver to an ADR and back
Write a Jest rendering test for the file-panel component confirming no edit controls are present when an ADR is displayed
Verify the full frontend test suite, including ArchUnitTS fitness functions, passes within the ten-minute build budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build, ADR-0016)
